theory.intro: Annuity problems use the future value formula $FV = a\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ in reverse to calculate required periodic contributions, the time needed to reach a financial target, or to compare different investment options.
facts: To find the regular payment $a$ needed for a target future value, solve $a = \dfrac{FV \times r}{(1+r)^{n}-1}$.
To find the number of periods $n$, rearrange for $(1+r)^{n}$ and take logarithms of both sides.
Increasing the interest rate or lengthening the duration increases future value exponentially due to compounding.
Doubling the term more than doubles the final balance because accumulated interest compounds over longer time.
steps: State the future value formula $FV = a\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ and substitute the known values.
Rearrange algebraically for the unknown quantity ($a$ or $n$).
Evaluate and round to the required precision or the next whole period.

foundation.question_text: Jack wishes to save $\$15\,000$ in $4\text{ years}$ by making equal annual deposits at the end of each year into an account paying $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Calculate the required annual deposit $a$, correct to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **State the future value formula $FV = a\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ and substitute the known values.**
$15000 = a\left[\dfrac{1.05^{4}-1}{0.05}\right]$
2. **Rearrange algebraically for the unknown quantity ($a$ or $n$).**
$15000 = a \times 4.310125$
$a = \dfrac{15000}{4.310125}$
3. **Evaluate and round to the required precision or the next whole period.**
$= \$3480.18$

foundation.question_text: A business needs $\$50\,000$ in $5\text{ years}$ to upgrade company vehicles. The funds will be accumulated with quarterly deposits at the end of each quarter into an account paying $6\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. Find the required quarterly payment.
Hannah deposits $\$400$ at the end of each month into an annuity earning $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. How many whole months will it take for the balance to first exceed $\$20\,000$?
foundation.solution_text:
1. **State the future value formula $FV = a\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ and substitute the known values.**
$r = \dfrac{0.072}{12} = 0.006$
$20000 = 400\left[\dfrac{1.006^{n}-1}{0.006}\right]$
2. **Rearrange algebraically for the unknown quantity ($a$ or $n$).**
$120 = 400(1.006^{n}-1)$
$0.3 = 1.006^{n}-1$
$1.006^{n} = 1.3$
$n = \dfrac{\ln(1.3)}{\ln(1.006)}$
3. **Evaluate and round to the required precision or the next whole period.**
$n \approx 43.84$
$= 44\text{ months}$

foundation.question_text: Oliver invests $\$2000$ at the end of each year at $8\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Find the number of years $n$ needed for the total investment to exceed $\$40\,000$.

Plan A involves saving $\$1200$ per year for $10\text{ years}$ at $6\%$ p.a. Plan B involves saving $\$600$ per year for $20\text{ years}$ at $6\%$ p.a. Both plans deposit $\$12\,000$ in total. Calculate which plan yields the higher future value and find the difference.

An investor deposits $\$500$ at the end of each month into an annuity. Calculate the future value after $8\text{ years}$ at: (a) $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, and (b) $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Find how much more interest is earned at the higher rate.

A family wants to accumulate $\$30\,000$ in $6\text{ years}$ for home renovations by making equal monthly payments into an account earning $5.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Calculate the required monthly payment.

development.question_text: A manufacturing firm requires $\$250\,000$ in $8\text{ years}$ to replace factory machinery. A sinking fund pays $6.8\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly. Calculate the half-yearly contribution required at the end of each period.

A saver deposits $\$750$ at the end of each quarter into an annuity paying $6\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. Determine the number of complete quarters required for the balance to reach at least $\$35\,000$.

Maya wants to save $\$80\,000$ for a home deposit in $7\text{ years}$. She compares investing $\$750$ per month at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly versus $\$850$ per month at $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Determine which option achieves a higher balance and calculate the difference.

An individual aims to build a retirement nest egg of $\$500\,000$ over $25\text{ years}$ with monthly contributions earning $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Calculate the required monthly contribution $a$.
A student deposits $\$100$ at the end of each month into an investment earning $9.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. How many months are required to accumulate $\$5000$?

Lucas has a choice of saving $\$4000$ at the end of each year for $15\text{ years}$ or $\$2000$ at the end of each year for $30\text{ years}$, both earning $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Find the difference in total interest earned between the two options.
To accumulate $\$120\,000$ in $12\text{ years}$ at $6.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, calculate the required monthly contribution to the nearest cent.

mastery.question_text: An investor needs $\$1\,000\,000$ upon retiring in $30\text{ years}$. She can invest in Fund A at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly or Fund B at $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Calculate the monthly contribution required for each fund and find how much less she needs to deposit each month with Fund B.

A superannuation account has monthly contributions of $\$500$ earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Find: (a) the time $n_{1}$ in whole months to reach $\$100\,000$, and (b) the additional time $n_{2}-n_{1}$ in whole months to grow from $\$100\,000$ to $\$200\,000$.

Emma starts saving $\$300$ per month at age $25$ for $15\text{ years}$ (until age $40$) and then leaves the accumulated balance to compound untouched without further deposits until age $65$ ($25\text{ years}$ of compounding). Liam starts saving $\$300$ per month at age $40$ and continues until age $65$ ($25\text{ years}$ of continuous deposits). If both earn $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, determine who has the larger balance at age $65$ and find the difference.
